profiles.meeting_scenario: A staff engineer and a product manager at a developer-tools startup are holding a 10-day brainstorming meeting to shape a prototype for an internal 'vibe coding' feature in their hosted IDE. The company wants a demo for an upcoming platform review, showing how developers can describe both intent and desired software feel and receive runnable scaffolds plus iterative refinements. The agenda is to generate candidate prototype directions, narrow them to 2-3 viable concepts, and agree on what a lightweight demo should include. The expected outcome is a short list of brainstormed concepts and an apparent shared plan for a 'thin vertical slice' demo that can be shown to leadership without a full product commitment.

members.name: Priya Natarajan
members.expertise: LLM orchestration, IDE integrations, rapid prototyping, internal platform architecture
members.background: Priya previously built code-assist features at a cloud tooling company and now leads exploratory engineering spikes for AI-native workflows inside the startup's browser-based IDE.
members.private_state: Priya wants the brainstorm to converge on a technically contained prototype she can build with one engineer in under two weeks, while avoiding any dependency on account-level policy changes or production-grade reliability commitments.
hidden_assumptions: A 'demo' should run inside the existing internal sandbox workspace with stubbed services rather than touching real customer repositories or deployment paths.
A 'thin vertical slice' means one end-to-end path for a single happy-case app template, even if the surrounding controls and edge cases are simulated.
If they say 'interactive feedback loop,' it is acceptable for the loop to happen within one IDE session with ephemeral state and no long-term project memory.
Using the 'existing safety layer' means reusing the current prompt moderation and code-scan wrappers already wired into the internal assistant, without introducing new governance review.
When people say the feature should feel 'personalized,' a few selectable style presets are enough for the prototype; true per-user learned adaptation is out of scope.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.role: Senior Product Manager, AI Coding Surfaces
members.expertise: developer workflows, product framing, executive demos, go-to-market experimentation
members.background: Lucas came from a low-code platform vendor and now owns early product definition for AI-assisted coding experiences aimed at expanding the company's enterprise footprint.
members.private_state: Lucas wants the brainstorm to produce a concept that appears strategically broad enough for leadership and pilot customers, signaling product differentiation and future enterprise readiness rather than just a technical toy.
hidden_assumptions: A 'demo' should resemble something that could plausibly be shown to design partners on their own repos soon after the platform review, even if some pieces are still manually supported.
A 'thin vertical slice' means the user journey is complete from prompt to generated project to commit-ready artifact, with visible trust and audit affordances around it.
If they say 'interactive feedback loop,' it includes continuity across multiple revisions over at least a project session so users can refine intent over time.
Using the 'existing safety layer' presumes whatever baseline enterprise guardrails leadership already expects for externally previewable AI features, including traceability of generated changes.
When people say the feature should feel 'personalized,' it should adapt to the team's conventions or repository context rather than only offering generic style modes.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a thin vertical slice
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to aim for a 'thin vertical slice' for the vibe coding demo.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means a narrowly scoped end-to-end prototype in the internal IDE that handles one curated happy-path app generation flow with mocked or sandboxed integrations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means a minimal but complete user journey that looks externally credible, including commit-ready output and visible product surfaces that suggest near-term pilot readiness.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to using 'thin vertical slice' as a positive shorthand for disciplined scoping, so the phrase signals alignment and neither feels a need to unpack whether completeness refers to engineering path coverage or product journey coverage.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the interactive feedback loop
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss including an 'interactive feedback loop' in the prototype.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya assumes the loop is confined to one live coding session in which the user asks for a revision, the agent regenerates, and the state can be discarded afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas assumes the loop includes continuity across several iterations tied to the same project context, so the system appears to remember prior intent refinements and evolving taste.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase comes directly from the seed framing and sounds inherently high-level; both consider some kind of back-and-forth obviously necessary, so neither thinks to specify the persistence boundary of that loop during brainstorming.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of using the existing safety layer
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the prototype should 'sit behind the existing safety layer.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya presupposes this refers to the current internal moderation prompts, code scanning hooks, and sandbox restrictions already available for employee-only experiments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas presupposes this refers to the baseline governance package leadership associates with features that could be shown to pilot customers, including provenance views and an auditable record of generated changes.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither frames this as an open decision because each believes the organization already has a shared meaning for 'existing safety layer'; the term functions as organizational shorthand that usually goes unchallenged.

misalignment_points.topic: What personalization means in vibe coding
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the experience should feel 'personalized' rather than generic.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya believes personalization is achieved if the prototype lets users choose or infer a few vibe presets such as 'minimal,' 'playful,' or 'enterprise-clean' that affect generated scaffolding and copy.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas believes personalization requires the system to reflect project or team conventions, such as repo structure, naming norms, or prior feedback, so users feel it understands their actual working context.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a brainstorming setting, 'personalized' sounds like an aspirational product adjective rather than a measurable requirement, so both can enthusiastically endorse it while silently applying different thresholds for what would satisfy the claim.

The key is proving the core interaction without inviting policy or reliability scope.
